races.name: ROA/RSA Shared Ownership Day Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Tellherthename
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner at OR 138 and a recent course-and-distance winner on good ground, handled well by Dan Skelton's yard (10 wins from 27 in 14 days); carrying 164lbs as top weight could blunt its finish, and its style-fit tag suggests it is racing outside its most natural comfort zone, but uncontested lead in a field of three is a significant compensator.
runners_data.comment: Landed back-to-back races most recently, including a six-length success at Uttoxeter off a lower mark, and remains well treated against his hurdle form; he likes to bowl along at the front and today's distance suits, with his trainer firing at a remarkable 50%.

runners_data.name: Captain Cool
runners_data.note: Strong recent profile with four placings from five runs on similar going (11/13 sim-going strike rate) including two wins and two seconds, and the 3lb apprentice claim from Luke Scott is a meaningful advantage at the weights; a natural prominent type who should sit comfortably in second, ready to pounce if the leader is caught flat-footed at the last.
runners_data.comment: In good heart over recent starts, with a 21-length win at Plumpton from a lower mark three runs back and second last time at just 1lb below today's official rating; first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces could sharpen him further.

runners_data.name: Ice In The Veins
runners_data.note: Trainer Sarah-Jayne Davies is 0-from-3 in the past fortnight and the horse's recent form reads poorly (P2 in last two, with a pulled-up run), though it does handle good ground; in reality a front-running type rather than a hold-up horse — it has been mapped rearward only because the field offers no true backmarkers — so expect it to race prominently regardless of its listed position.
runners_data.comment: Stepped up on his debut for the yard with a solid second at Uttoxeter last time, beaten six lengths; he acts on good ground and over today's trip, and is likely to show more once he learns to settle.

races.paceDynamic: Tellherthename is the confirmed pace-setter here and, in a field of just three, will establish the tempo from the front on good-to-firm ground at Stratford without any meaningful pressure from rivals. Captain Cool and Ice In The Veins are both naturally prominent types who will track Tellherthename closely rather than stretching the pace from behind, meaning this shapes into a controlled, single-file procession with a modest early gallop. The race is unlikely to develop any real tempo until the turn for home, where the small field and lack of a pressing rival means Tellherthename can dictate entirely on its own terms. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-front horses that travel well and can quicken off a steady pace — late closers and true hold-up profiles have no meaningful role in a three-runner, uncontested-pace scenario. The field is stacked with prominent types and none are natural hold-up horses, so all three are effectively competing for the same ground positions; Tellherthename is best placed to secure the lead, with Captain Cool likely to hold the rails tracker spot.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tellherthename Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Tellherthename dictates a sustainable, uncontested lead and rations the effort to the final fence.
scenarios.body: If Tellherthename dictates a sustainable, uncontested lead and rations the effort to the final fence.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swamps Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Captain Cool tracks the pace economically and produces a well-timed challenge from the last fence.
scenarios.body: If Captain Cool tracks the pace economically and produces a well-timed challenge from the last fence.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Ice In The Veins Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late and Ice In The Veins, running freer than its mapped position suggests, picks up the pieces.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses late and Ice In The Veins, running freer than its mapped position suggests, picks up the pieces.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Jumping Error Scrambles Result
scenarios.trigger: If a fencing mistake by the leader or a rival disrupts the race order at a critical late fence.
scenarios.body: If a fencing mistake by the leader or a rival disrupts the race order at a critical late fence.

watchPoints.text: Tellherthename carries 164lbs on quick ground and any sign of laboured jumping late could allow Captain Cool to quicken past at the final fence.
All three runners are naturally prominent types — watch for an awkward bunching moment on the first circuit at Stratford's tight bends, which could cause interference or a costly mistake.
Ice In The Veins' pulled-up run in recent form is a significant flag; monitor its jumping in the early stages, as a repeat exit would reduce this to a two-horse race immediately.

Captain Cool's apprentice jockey Luke Scott claiming 3lbs brings it closest to Tellherthename at the weights — if the pace is even moderately strong, this weight relief could prove the difference in a tight finish.

Good-to-firm conditions at Stratford favour quick, economical jumping — Tellherthename's sim-going record of only 3W4P at this level of going is worth noting against Captain Cool's superior 3W10P sample.

races.name: Racehorse Ownership From 25 Pound At racingclub.com Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Colibri Bleu
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old fitted with headgear, last seen just 14 days ago finishing in the pack; style is unclassified and trainer T Ellis has a winless T14 record of 0/4, limiting confidence in a yard in form.|
runners_data.comment: Clearly pulling hard in his latest start at this course, where he was well beaten; a first-time hood could help settle him over the 2m trip, but with multiple pull-ups in his recent record he needs to show considerably more here.

runners_data.name: Connemara Joe
runners_data.note: Consistent without winning — has shown placed form on good ground — but a 766P-4 recent form string suggests he finds a way to be there without ever getting his head in front; no obvious angle to upgrade.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten 35 lengths on his hurdles debut at Warwick and brings only modest point-to-point form to this; he ranks among the lower-rated in the field and there is little in the record to suggest improvement here.

runners_data.name: King Troy
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old returning from 479 days off (39 days P-mark), last seen pulled up; his natural hold-up style is stretched by a pace map that pushes him into midfield, and a lengthy absence compounds the concern significantly.|
runners_data.comment: Managed just one horse behind him on his hurdles introduction last year, and his subsequent outings have included pull-ups and an unseating; there is nothing to build on from either his point form or his jumping record under rules, and all the improvement must come now.

runners_data.name: Mr Rafiki
runners_data.note: Jonjo O'Neill Jr is an upgrade in the saddle for this consistent if placed performer, and the horse has handled similar good ground before; that said, his true sit-and-wait style is compromised here because the race is unlikely to produce the searching gallop he needs.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent in his three hurdle starts, he acts on today's going and trip and tries a first-time tongue-tie; could prove a bigger threat at a shorter distance and may be the type capable of better than his maiden form suggests.

runners_data.name: Penzance
runners_data.note: Better form on longer trips than this field brings — a second over 18f on good ground is the standout piece — but a 5lb claim jockey on a horse whose true hold-up style is squeezed by pace-map crowding makes this a tricky ride tactically.|
runners_data.comment: Showed more over a longer trip at this course last time and is unexposed enough over hurdles to continue developing; his best flat form has come entirely on the all-weather, and the trainer's yard is yet to fire in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Usyk
runners_data.note: The most interesting of the hold-up brigade given a placed effort at 18f on good ground and consistent form; ridden by an amateur claimer which tempers the handicapping advantage, but this horse has the profile to improve if the race unfolds with any early zip.|
runners_data.comment: Course and distance experience is in his favour, and the last outing was below his best — he should come on considerably from it; a trip and going within his range, and the type to step forward.

runners_data.name: Bound For Glory
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race and winner last time out over a similar trip on good ground — this is the horse who shapes the entire race; a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.90 is noted but he is simply doing his natural job here, and Ciaran Gethings rode him to that win.|
runners_data.comment: Won his maiden bumper at this course by 76 lengths last time on faster ground, a performance that showed real potential; there is every reason to expect progression into hurdling now, though the step up in class is the question to answer.

runners_data.name: Square d'Alboni
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's T14 figure of 10/27 is comfortably the strongest trainer angle in the race, and Harry Skelton gives this hold-up type every chance of being produced at exactly the right moment; the 151-day break is the only question mark.|
runners_data.comment: A useful flat performer now with a top yard after a breathing operation, he shapes as one with considerably more to offer over hurdles; the last run at Catterick, where he bled, can be set aside, and his trainer is among the busiest in form.

races.paceDynamic: Bound For Glory is the sole confirmed front-runner and, on Good to Firm ground at Stratford, will set a sustainable gallop from the front without any genuine challenger to his position. With Penzance, Mr Rafiki, and King Troy all natural hold-up types pushed forward on the pace map due to overcrowding at the rear, the reality is that Bound For Glory faces no genuine pace pressure and can dictate terms entirely on his own terms. The field holds more hold-up and midfield types than the race shape can naturally accommodate — Penzance, Mr Rafiki, and King Troy are the horses most likely to be shuffled away from their preferred positions, compromising their chances. This controlled, single-paced gallop on quick ground strongly favours the horse who can travel prominently, jump fluently, and sustain his effort through the final exchanges — a profile that suits front-runners and prominent racers who stay on under pressure rather than late-finishing hold-up types who need a truly run race to deliver their best.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bound For Glory Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Bound For Glory bowls along in front unchallenged and sets a fair but uncontested gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: If Bound For Glory bowls along in front unchallenged and sets a fair but uncontested gallop throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Square d'Alboni tracks Bound For Glory closely and kicks turning in, forcing a sustained duel.
scenarios.body: If Square d'Alboni tracks Bound For Glory closely and kicks turning in, forcing a sustained duel.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely strong enough to set up a late run for one of the hold-up types who finds their natural position.
scenarios.body: If the gallop is genuinely strong enough to set up a late run for one of the hold-up types who finds their natural position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or fallers disrupt the race shape and reduce the contest to a war of attrition in the home straight.
scenarios.body: If jumping errors or fallers disrupt the race shape and reduce the contest to a war of attrition in the home straight.

watchPoints.text: Bound For Glory has no pace rival — watch for him to control the fractions from flag to finish and if he jumps cleanly at the first three hurdles he could prove very hard to peg back.
Square d'Alboni is the one horse with both jockey and trainer form to challenge Bound For Glory late — watch for Harry Skelton to position him second or third from the outset rather than holding up.

King Troy's 479-day absence combined with a pull-up last time should be closely monitored in the paddock and at the start — any sign of reluctance or ring-rustiness would make him a definite risk to oppose.

Penzance, Mr Rafiki, and King Troy are all being asked to race closer to the pace than their natural style dictates — if any one of them overcooks it early and ties up in the straight, it could create interference for those tracking behind.

The Good to Firm ground (confirmed across all races on the card) will put a premium on clean jumping and economical travel — any horse that makes a significant error at a hurdle on this surface is likely to lose far more ground than on softer going.

races.name: SolidCAM UK Partner Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Jackstell
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner wearing tongue strap who gets to lead without a challenger at 2m6f on a surface he handles (7 sim-going runs) — the concern is whether 168lbs and a 6th-place last run signal he is on a downward curve despite his natural positional advantage here.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in his last five starts show real ability, though his progress has stalled of late; he goes in first-time cheekpieces at a trip and on going that should suit, but held comfortably at Market Rasen last time.

runners_data.name: Snatch A Glance
runners_data.note: Fergal O'Brien's consistent mare has an excellent going record (8/8 on similar ground), handles the 2m6f trip based on recent runs at 20f, and races prominently — with fewer natural rivals for prominent positions than normal, she has a better chance of getting a clean racing position here.
runners_data.comment: Ran close to form when beaten three lengths at Market Rasen last time and a sound surface clearly suits; however, his trainer is badly out of form, he sits among the lower-rated in the field, and more improvement is needed here.

runners_data.name: Balboa
runners_data.note: Front-running type with Seamus Mullins who won at 2m4f last time out on soft ground; the switch to good-to-firm and a step back up to 2m6f are legitimate questions, and his sim-going record (0 wins from 6 on comparable surfaces) is a flag worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Won convincingly at Ayr from a lower mark to show he retains ability, but he was outpaced and beaten 21 lengths last time off this same official rating; a tricky ride at best and hard to trust here.

runners_data.name: Tyson
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's gelding is a genuine hold-up horse — not mapped rearward by crowd pressure — with a win and a second from two completed runs at today's trip, and Harry Skelton's ability to place horses late off a steady pace is the key tactical lever in this race.
runners_data.comment: Back in form since changing yards, landing a 10-length win at Huntingdon off a lower mark; he goes well over today's trip and going, remains generously treated on his best form, and his trainer is firing well.

runners_data.name: Prince De Juilley
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner with headgear (p) who has been consistently placed in big-field races, but this field's prominent glut means he is unlikely to get his preferred position and will race in a less effective midfield slot; his sim-going figures (12/15 runs, 1 win, 6 places) are excellent if the position issue resolves.
runners_data.comment: In form over hurdles with a string of placed efforts before the latest, he wears first-time cheekpieces and the trip and ground suit well; tiring late at Worcester on his comeback suggests he can build on that now.

runners_data.name: Lion Of The Desert
runners_data.note: Headgear-wearing (h) type from Grace Harris whose true preference is to race prominently — he has won twice from 15 similar-ground starts but faces the same positional squeeze as Prince De Juilley, meaning his chance depends on an outcome that requires him to be comfortable racing wide or without cover in midfield.
runners_data.comment: Wearing a first-time hood, he has won at Ffos Las and been narrowly beaten in his two most recent outings over course and distance; on the upgrade and clearly at home on the going, though he faces a 3lb higher official mark than when last placed.

runners_data.name: The Gypsy Davey
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse for the amateur Mr B T Stone (7lb claim) with 14/15 sim-going runs suggesting he handles the surface thoroughly; the visor (v) is habitual and he has finished fourth in his last two runs over comparable trips, but his ceiling at OR 100 in this company is an honest question.
runners_data.comment: Wears a visor for the first time and goes well when allowed to front-run on a sound surface at a trip that suits; yet to score in recent outings, and that distant fourth at Hereford will need to be set aside for him to get involved.

runners_data.name: Minella Double
runners_data.note: 130-day absence for Rob Summers' eight-year-old is a significant concern, and his form string features two pullings-up; headgear (t) is worn regularly, his true running style is hold-up despite appearing in midfield on the map, and the race fitness question makes him the hardest to assess with confidence in the field.
runners_data.comment: Back after a lengthy absence — his last outing ended in a pulled-up effort at Warwick after bleeding — he now tries a first-time tongue-tie and acts well at around this trip on good ground; his inconsistency in recent starts remains the main reservation.

races.paceDynamic: Jackstell is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should settle into a comfortable, uncontested gallop over 2m6f on good-to-firm ground at Stratford. That kind of controlled, solo lead means the pace is likely to be honest but not punishing — Jackstell sets the terms entirely on his own schedule, and the race will be run at a measured rhythm until the tempo inevitably increases in the final mile. The field contains an unusually high concentration of prominent-racing types — Prince De Juilley, Lion Of The Desert, and Snatch A Glance among them — and they cannot all occupy the positions they want, meaning some will race in unnatural midfield slots and be disadvantaged by it. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses or those with a clean cruising speed who can travel kindly in a compact pack and produce a sustained run from the home turn; Tyson, as a genuine hold-up type partnered by Harry Skelton in a field where prominent runners are congested and compromised, fits that profile most squarely.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jackstell Controls, Stays True
scenarios.trigger: If Jackstell bowls along uncontested and the pace proves sufficient to stretch the field before the last.
scenarios.body: If Jackstell bowls along uncontested and the pace proves sufficient to stretch the field before the last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Skelton Times Late Run
scenarios.trigger: If the pace from Jackstell is steady enough that Tyson travels superbly in rear and Skelton produces him with a perfectly timed challenge from the home turn.
scenarios.body: If the pace from Jackstell is steady enough that Tyson travels superbly in rear and Skelton produces him with a perfectly timed challenge from the home turn.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Logjam Unravels
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of promoted prominent types — Prince De Juilley, Lion Of The Desert — fail to settle in unnatural midfield positions and inject pace into the race, lifting the tempo sharply.
scenarios.body: If the cluster of promoted prominent types — Prince De Juilley, Lion Of The Desert — fail to settle in unnatural midfield positions and inject pace into the race, lifting the tempo sharply.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely in the final stages and those ridden with restraint — including Minella Double — produce sustained late runs.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses entirely in the final stages and those ridden with restraint — including Minella Double — produce sustained late runs.

watchPoints.text: Tyson — Harry Skelton is live to produce him from a genuine hold-up position with a perfectly timed run; watch how quickly Skelton commits him from the home turn if Jackstell has the race at a meander.

Prince De Juilley and Lion Of The Desert — both natural prominent racers are mapped to midfield by field pressure; if either fails to settle or starts to work hard to maintain contact, expect their challenges to weaken from the third-last hurdle.

Jackstell's weight burden of 168lbs combined with a most-recent run of 6th and a trainer who is 1/8 in the last 14 days — the uncontested lead is an asset, but the horse must be able to sustain it over 2m6f on this lively surface.

Minella Double's absence of 130 days should be tracked in pre-race: if he shows signs of freshness or racing lazily out of the gate, his chance either rises sharply (fit) or evaporates early (unready).

Snatch A Glance — the combination of an apprentice claim (Fern O'Brien, 5lb) and a trainer at 0/6 in 14 days cuts both ways; monitor how she is ridden early, as a horse with her prominent profile needs a clean start in a contested midfield.

races.name: Davisons Law Moving You Forward Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Zhang Fei
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with strong good-ground credentials (11/15 runs on similar going) and Fergal O'Brien's yard has Fern O'Brien (5) claiming; suited by this 2m2½f trip and the relaxed tempo that Newport will likely create, though a tendency to finish mid-division (recent 3rd best effort) suggests needs everything to go right late.|
runners_data.comment: Shaped encouragingly at Cartmel last time, moving smoothly but failing to find the extra gear when pressed, finishing 9½ lengths third in a handicap hurdle; effective at 2m but form has been patchy of late and a trainer out of form is a further concern.

runners_data.name: Newport
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner who will control the pace from flag to finish; Iain Jardine in decent 14-day form and the 9-day turnaround is not a concern for a hold-all policy horse — this horse won last time and slots in here at OR 98, but note the STYLE_FIT flag means if forced off a lead it loses its main asset.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap at Hexham by 5½ lengths last time, thriving on a demanding test of the trip and acting well on good ground; clearly in fine form for his new yard and runs in first-time blinkers, with scope to carry on from a mark that looks live.

runners_data.name: Get The Value
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up type (8yo) whose recent form string includes two pulled-up efforts and a string of mid-division finishes; good-ground form exists but the trainer (T14: 3/5 in a small sample) and Nick Slatter's claim may not be enough to overcome a profile that screams out-of-form.|
runners_data.comment: Out of form after being pulled up at Newton Abbot on his latest start, the most recent in a run of poor performances; showed better ability last summer but his current mark now looks above what he can deliver in his present state.

runners_data.name: Charlie My Boy
runners_data.note: Strong course profile on good ground (14/15 sim-going runs, three wins) and ran second last time over 2m4f — James Davies is an experienced jockey who can position close to the pace, meaning Charlie My Boy need not rely on a late sprint; at 9yo the fitness angle matters and 36 days off is worth monitoring.|
runners_data.comment: Shaped with credit at Huntingdon last time, moving into contention before being overhauled close home by a well-weighted rival; handles today's trip and going well and his overall mark looks fair enough, with more to offer on the back of that run.

runners_data.name: Western Soldier
runners_data.note: Genuine deep closer by nature whose true running style has him at the rear, though with five hold-up types ahead of him on the map he will find it hard to get the wide, unobstructed late run he needs; best going figures (7/15 on similar) are modest and recent form (4th and 5th) doesn't inspire confidence in this tempo.|
runners_data.comment: Had his chance at Worcester last time and ran to his level, finishing 9¼ lengths back in a handicap hurdle; acts on good ground at 2m and the rating edge is workable if he builds on that recent outing and shows greater consistency.

runners_data.name: Katzoff
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton's mount (Dan Skelton T14: 10/27 in excellent form) is the yard's main hope, but Katzoff is a genuine hold-up horse who cannot manufacture a prominent position in this field — strong going record (14/15 on similar ground) gives him viability if gaps appear late, but OR 81 marks a career that has struggled for consistency.|
runners_data.comment: Switches to a yard in fine current form for his British debut, with his best Irish form suggesting today's mark is workable; he set too strong a pace and found little in the tank at the finish last time, but better tactics should give a truer reflection.

runners_data.name: Yanka Blue
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who brings youth and low weight (149lbs) to the table; a natural hold-up type who has hit the frame twice on good-to-soft at a lower level, but being mapped forward from the rear means Barry John Murphy's horse will not get its natural rhythm in this crowded hold-up group.|
runners_data.comment: Showed her best form earlier in the season when placed on a couple of occasions, but has tailed off recently and went too freely at Newton Abbot last time before fading; she handles today's trip and has enough ability to feature but inconsistency has been an issue.

runners_data.name: Stellarmasterpiece
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 2m on good ground, wears a hood (headgear positive), and Sean Bowen gives this a serious look from a prominent style that suits the one-pace-setter scenario perfectly; Micky Hammond's yard (T14: 1/11) is quiet but the horse's own form is the compelling factor here.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap here last time by 2¼ lengths off a lower mark, though the success owed something to fortune when a rival departed late; she handles this trip and going, runs in first-time cheekpieces, and her Flat background suggests more could yet be drawn out over hurdles.

runners_data.name: Winston's Oath
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with limited hurdles experience (recent 3rd and 9th) who is a true hold-up horse shuffled toward midfield on the map by the field's composition; going figures are poor (4/8 on similar) and the youth advantage is offset by inexperience in competitive handicap company.|
runners_data.comment: Struggled at Uttoxeter last time, fading into the back of the field after a string of jumping mistakes in a handicap hurdle; he handles good ground at 2m and is still finding his feet in handicap company, though a trainer badly out of form does not help his case.

runners_data.name: Brooklyn Lullaby
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby yard has been busy (T14: 5/40) and Harry Bannister takes the ride, but this horse carries the lowest OR (72) and its hold-up style — displaced forward on the map — means it cannot operate from its natural position; recent form (5th last time, no wins in last five) offers little encouragement.|
runners_data.comment: Still relatively unexposed in this sphere and capable of better, she was never brought into contention at Southwell last time after a break, finishing 6 lengths off the pace; acts on good ground at 2m and should come forward for that outing.

races.paceDynamic: Newport is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground at Stratford over 2m2½f. Tom Midgley takes the ride and the Iain Jardine yard has been in form (9/34 over 14 days), so Newport is likely to cruise along at a measured tempo rather than blasting off suicidally — creating a race that rewards those who can travel smoothly in behind and produce a clean finishing effort. Stellarmasterpiece adds a second prominent type from a handy position, meaning the lead duo could stretch the field if Newport presses on, but the overall tempo is unlikely to be frenetic. This shape strongly favours hold-up horses with proven good-ground form who can pick off a pacemaker who has had an uncontested lead — Charlie My Boy and Zhang Fei profile well, but the field is saturated with closers, many of whom cannot all settle as far back as their natural style demands. Several runners listed as hold-up types — Western Soldier, Katzoff, Yanka Blue, Winston's Oath, and Brooklyn Lullaby — are true deep closers who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because there are simply more hold-up horses than rear slots; the horses most likely to actually secure a prominent position behind Newport are Stellarmasterpiece and potentially Charlie My Boy, who has the tactical profile to travel close to the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Newport Dictates, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Newport is allowed a soft, uncontested lead and the midfield-to-rear runners can produce a clean late run on drying ground.
scenarios.body: If Newport is allowed a soft, uncontested lead and the midfield-to-rear runners can produce a clean late run on drying ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stellarmasterpiece Tracks And Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Stellarmasterpiece travels prominently behind Newport, jumps fluently throughout and sustains his effort to collar the leader before the last.
scenarios.body: If Stellarmasterpiece travels prominently behind Newport, jumps fluently throughout and sustains his effort to collar the leader before the last.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Newport Outstays The Field
scenarios.trigger: If Newport bowls along in front, the pace is genuinely steady, and none of the hold-up horses get a clear enough run to reel him in.
scenarios.body: If Newport bowls along in front, the pace is genuinely steady, and none of the hold-up horses get a clear enough run to reel him in.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is artificially slow early, the race turns into a sprint from two out and the smaller weights and younger legs come into play.
scenarios.body: If the tempo is artificially slow early, the race turns into a sprint from two out and the smaller weights and younger legs come into play.

watchPoints.text: Newport's unchallenged lead is the race's pivot point — if anything forces it wider or pressures it early, the entire pace shape collapses and hold-up horses lose their primary target.|

Stellarmasterpiece's hood and the Bowen booking are a compound signal worth monitoring in the market; if it drifts, suspect the prominent position cannot be held, but if it firms it becomes the key tactical rival to Newport.|

Charlie My Boy's 36-day absence and veteran status (9yo) mean fitness on the day is a genuine question — watch the pre-race demeanour and sweating in the paddock before committing to the good-ground form figures.|

The going is officially Good To Firm at Stratford across all races tonight — confirmed by multiple race-by-race reports — which consistently favours horses with proven form on a sound surface; any runner with a CONCERN tag would need reassessing, but none are flagged here.|

With five genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield, traffic management is a real risk in the straight — jockeys on Katzoff (Skelton), Western Soldier (Pritchard) and Brooklyn Lullaby (Bannister) will need to find daylight simultaneously, raising the probability of interference or a blocked run for at least one of them.|

races.name: Laura Horsfall Racing Club Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Lady Kara
runners_data.note: Three wins from her last four starts on good ground over similar trips underscore her current form, and Luke Scott's (3) claim brings her weight down further — in her natural front-running role on going she handles well, she is the chief interest in the race shape analysis.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in her last five starts, most recently landing a novice hurdle at Newton Abbot under pressure; the step up in trip on her chase debut should play to her strengths and she runs in first-time hood and tongue-tie, with a trainer in temporarily poor form the main reservation.

runners_data.name: Therhythmofthenite
runners_data.note: Tom Cannon takes the ride on a horse who has placed twice at around 2m3f on good ground but whose form figures of 483-3 suggest inconsistency; a prominent racing style means she will be the closest pursuer to Lady Kara, though her 0W1P record at similar going is a mild concern.
runners_data.comment: Made a string of jumping mistakes and faded on his chase debut at Warwick, finishing well beaten; he has scope to do better over fences and wears first-time tongue-tie, though that introductory showing leaves questions to answer.

runners_data.name: Lakefield Flyer
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon's eight-year-old has strong course form (two runs in Ireland over comparable trips on good ground) and Paddy Hanlon's 5lb claim is attractive, though a hold-up style over a trip that may not produce the end-to-end gallop he needs is a limiting factor; his most recent run at 2m4f on good was a solid seventh.
runners_data.comment: Has chasing form that marks him out as a legitimate threat here, acting well at today's trip on a sound surface; first-time tongue-tie could help sharpen him up, though the question of whether he stayed at Hexham last time is the chief reservation alongside an inconsistent profile.

runners_data.name: Delpotro
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen is the standout jockey booking in this field and Delpotro's form — four placings from his last five starts including two seconds — suggests he runs his race consistently; a hold-up style means he is reliant on Lady Kara setting a hot enough pace, and with a controlled lead expected, the closing ground he needs may simply not materialise.
runners_data.comment: Has placed on several chase starts and handles today's going and trip well, with a mark that retains scope; a thumping defeat here last time when unable to control the pace is hard to ignore, and he is not wholly reliable, but runs in first-time tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Glenmalure Flyer
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's runner holds a genuine hold-up style in terms of natural racing pattern — mapped here to midfield simply because the field's rear is already crowded — and having run just four days ago (LR:4d) and with 10 winners in 27 days for the yard, freshness and trainer form are positive, though the out-of-role mapping means the position on the track may not suit.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap chase on her fencing debut at Bangor-on-Dee by 2¼ lengths last time, showing promising form as a point winner with more to give for a top yard; acts on good ground at 3m and runs in first-time tongue-tie, with only the quick turnaround to query.

runners_data.name: Thickthorn Tom
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner, so any race-day assessment is moot; his natural hold-up tendencies over similar trips on good ground made him a poor fit for a race likely to be run at a controlled tempo regardless, and the redistribution to midfield on the map reflects the overcrowded hold-up end of this field rather than his preferred racing position.

races.paceDynamic: Lady Kara is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, with no rival willing or able to press her from the front, she is set to stride into a comfortable, uncontested lead from the flag. Therhythmofthenite is the only other horse with prominent tendencies, but with Lady Kara already filling that lead role, Therhythmofthenite is likely to settle just off the pace rather than mount a sustained challenge for the front. The hold-up horses — Lakefield Flyer, Delpotro, Glenmalure Flyer and Thickthorn Tom — will travel in behind, relying on a strong gallop to close the gap, but with only one horse controlling the tempo at a sustainable clip, the pace may never be fierce enough to fully compromise Lady Kara's stamina reserves on good-to-firm ground. This field contains more genuine hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate in their natural position — Glenmalure Flyer and Thickthorn Tom are true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning the closing ground they need to make up may be even greater than it appears. This race shape strongly favours a prominent or front-running profile: a controlled gallop set by a lightly-weighted, in-form Lady Kara on ground she handles well gives hold-up horses a very difficult task, and those racing closer to the pace are best positioned to capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Lady Kara — watch for a clean jump at the first fence; if she leads fluently from flag-fall with no pressure, the entire race shape resolves into the dominant Scenario A and the race is effectively over as a tactical contest.

Thickthorn Tom is listed as a non-runner — confirm at the pre-race stage, as his withdrawal further reduces the hold-up population and makes the pace map even more one-dimensional in Lady Kara's favour.

Glenmalure Flyer ran just four days ago and is mapped away from his true hold-up position — watch whether Tristan Durrell attempts to push forward early, which would signal the horse is being ridden against type and could disrupt Lady Kara's uncontested lead.

Delpotro with Sean Bowen is the highest-quality jockey-horse combination among the hold-up horses — watch whether Bowen positions him closer than expected from the outset, which would be the clearest sign that the closing ground on offer is judged insufficient for a pure hold-up run.

The going for this race is effectively Good to Firm despite the declared Good — all six previous races on the card returned Good to Firm, which marginally favours Lady Kara's quick-ground record (10 of 11 similar-going runs placed) and could blunt the stamina of heavier-weighted hold-up horses late on.

races.name: Sunday 12th July Is Family Day Mares' NH Flat Race (Conditional/Amateurs) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Redbarn
runners_data.comment: Landed a bumper at Worcester by 1¼ lengths last time, going away comfortably at the finish; effective at 2m on good ground and the trainer in sharp form, she is well placed to defy the penalty on this step back up to the trip.

runners_data.name: Ocean Rose
runners_data.comment: Beaten well on debut at Newton Abbot, showing inexperience throughout rather than meaningful form; she has much to demonstrate before threatening at this level and faces a challenging task on her second start.

runners_data.name: Upton Fern
runners_data.comment: A daughter of Linda's Lad whose dam landed a bumper, she is also a half-sister to a useful staying performer; her racecourse debut here means she is best watched rather than backed at this stage.

runners_data.name: Cool Million
runners_data.comment: Caught the eye on her Southwell debut despite finishing 9¼ lengths back in a maiden bumper, handling the trip and going reasonably well despite showing inexperience; she is capable of better with that run behind her and this trip looks right for her.

runners_data.name: Frankie's Flame
runners_data.comment: A Waldgeist filly purchased as a breeze-up buy, she is out of a mare who showed useful ability on the Flat but arrives from a yard whose strengths lie more on the level than in bumpers; a demanding first assignment on her racecourse debut.

runners_data.name: Queens Glance
runners_data.comment: Caught the eye on debut at Worcester, rallying late once she found her stride despite finishing 16 lengths fourth in an Amateurs' bumper; acts at 2m on good and runs in first-time tongue-tie, with a trainer in fine form and clear room for improvement on the first run.

runners_data.name: Thetype Istitle
runners_data.comment: Has point-to-point experience, most recently runner-up 13 lengths back in a maiden at Tattersalls Farm; that contact time over jumps and scope for further progress make her an interesting player on her rules debut here.
